Subject: Recap: Dedicated GPU capacity & isolation needs (Greenfield Labs)

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I tried to capture your priorities and any open questions we agreed to own.

Summary of pain & goals
- Primary: move inference for multi-tenant recommender models off the shared cluster to a reserved, isolated pool for latency and compliance reasons.
- Latency target: p95 < 80ms for 0-2048 token requests.
- Availability target: 99.9% (SLA) for production traffic.
- Scale profile: steady baseline ~120 concurrent streams; expected burst up to ~360 for Black Friday-style events.
- Data isolation: VPC peering + customer-managed encryption keys required.

Proposed dedicated capacity (approximate)
- Reserved GPUs: 6 x A100-class equivalent instances in a dedicated pool
- Autoscale floor/ceiling: baseline 6 (reserved), burstable to 12 behind policy-based gating
- KV/prefix cache: per-VM local KV cache + optional shared cache for common prompt prefixes

Open technical questions we will validate
1) Can your network/security team accept our VPC peering checklist and flow logs? (you said procurement will share their SOC/Security contacts)
2) Confirm expected RPS distribution — we used the 120 concurrent estimate to size the pool; any upcoming spikes we should simulate?
3) Encryption: confirm KMS provider (you mentioned AWS KMS but wanted to validate HSM requirement).

Attachments I’m sharing: Redwood-MVP-dedicated-plan.pdf (capacity SKU and config options) and Redwood-SLA-draft-Redlined.docx (initial SLA language we can iterate on).

Next steps
- Sara: confirm procurement / security contact and target procurement timeline (you mentioned mid-April).
- Tom: share a short traffic sample (CSV or synthetic load profile) so Vivek can run a sizing run.
- Vivek + Aditya + me: we’ll produce a one-page reserved-capacity proposal and a pilot checklist by Thu 19 Mar.

If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag and I’ll update the doc. Otherwise I’ll circulate the proposal and a suggested contract cadence after we get the procurement contact.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap — this aligns with our internal notes. A few clarifications from our side:

Confirmations
- SLA: 99.9% is our target. We’ll need to see the SLA draft that handles failover to a secondary region and what remedies look like for sustained degradations.
- Isolation: VPC peering + customer KMS is non-negotiable. We will provide the KMS owner contact.

Questions / asks
1) Can you provide an example of the canary/pilot plan you typically run for a dedicated pool? We want to limit risk during cutover.
2) For burst capacity, do you support pre-warmed nodes or is cold spin-up part of the burst profile? We need to understand RTO for additional nodes.
3) Pricing: rough ballpark for reserved 6x GPU baseline + burst to 12 for 12 months (or guidance on what pricing bucket to expect) — we know you’ll follow up with a formal quote.

Procurement timeline
- We’ll loop in procurement/security next week (they sign off on baseline agreements). Target: internal approval by Apr 15, PO by Apr 30.

Tom will upload a 48-hour sample traffic trace to the shared folder by EOD tomorrow.

Sara
VP Engineering | Greenfield Labs
Sara Cho <sara.cho@greenfieldlabs.com>
